hints.title: Monotonic Length Feasibility
hints.text: If a duplicate substring of length L exists, any of its subsegments of length smaller than L is also duplicated. This monotonic property allows testing candidate lengths logarithmically rather than checking every length sequentially.

hints.title: Rolling Fingerprint Verification
hints.text: For a candidate length L, slide a window across the string and compute polynomial rolling hashes to detect duplicate occurrences in linear time.

hints.title: Binary Search Over Length
hints.text: Perform binary search on L in range [1, n - 1]. In the checking step, return the starting index of a duplicate if found. Adjust binary search boundaries accordingly.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all pairs of substrings takes O(N^3) time which times out for N = 30,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Binary search on length combined with rolling hash verification runs in O(N log N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize binary search on answer length and apply Rabin-Karp or Suffix Automaton.
complexity.notes: Using a large prime modulus such as (1 << 61) - 1 prevents hash collisions.
